description: Close documented limitation #4 (SCRIPTING.md line ~86): persist Rhai function pointers in saved script variables instead of silently skipping them. The variable serializer in src/scripting.rs (enc/Dec::value, encode_vars/decode_vars) uses a self-describing tag-byte format (tags 0=unit,1=bool,2=int,3=float,4=string,5=char,6=array,7=map,8=blob; anything else -> Err -> skipped). Rhai 1.26.1 FnPtr exposes fn_name(), is_curried(), and curry() (the captured arguments). A NAMED function pointer with no curried/captured state (Fn("name")) is well-defined to persist: store its name, and on load rebind it with FnPtr::new(name). A closure or a curried function pointer captures runtime state that cannot be meaningfully reconstructed on load; those remain unserializable and must be handled deterministically (skipped with the existing chat-message mechanism, with a clear reason). This is a self-contained change inside scripting.rs plus the SCRIPTING.md doc update. It is INDEPENDENT of FEAT-003 and could be parallelized, but run after FEAT-001 to keep a single clean test/clippy baseline.
steps: Read src/scripting.rs fully around the serialization block (enc ~line 432, Dec/value ~line 506, encode_vars ~line 545, decode_vars ~line 568) and the existing fnptr test (~line 711) that currently asserts a function-pointer variable is skipped. Confirm the Rhai FnPtr API available in 1.26.1 by checking imports and, if needed, `cargo doc`/the rhai source in the registry cache; specifically fn_name() -> &str, is_curried() -> bool, and the ability to construct a plain FnPtr by name (FnPtr::new(name) returns Result). Do NOT add or change any dependency.

In enc(): before the final catch-all `return Err(format!("a {} can't be saved", ...))`, add a branch that detects a FnPtr (via Dynamic::try_cast::<rhai::FnPtr>() on a clone, or the appropriate type check). If the FnPtr is NOT curried/closure-like (is_curried() == false and it has a resolvable name), write a NEW tag byte (9) followed by the length-prefixed function name (reuse the existing put_len + bytes convention). If it IS curried / a true closure that captures state, return an Err with a clear message like 'a closure that captures state can't be saved' so it is skipped-and-reported exactly as today.

In Dec::value(): add a case for tag 9 that reads the length-prefixed name and reconstructs a function pointer with FnPtr::new(name) (map any error to a decode error string), returning it as a Dynamic. Keep MAX_DEPTH and bounds handling consistent with the other cases.

Ensure the format stays backward/forward compatible: tag 9 is new and additive; existing saves (tags 0-8) decode unchanged, and a save written by this version is only read by this version or newer. Confirm decode_vars still errors cleanly (not panics) on an unknown tag from a hypothetical newer version (the existing catch-all `t => Err(...)` already covers this).

Update the existing fnptr test and ADD tests in the scripting.rs #[cfg(test)] mod: (a) a NAMED function pointer variable round-trips through encode_vars/decode_vars and, after decode, is still callable / has the same fn_name(); (b) a true closure (|x| x+1) or a curried FnPtr is still skipped and reported via encode_vars' skipped list with a descriptive reason; (c) a map/array CONTAINING a named FnPtr nested inside round-trips (exercises the recursive enc/value path). Make assertions concrete (names, skipped count, skipped message substring).

Update SCRIPTING.md: change the 'What can't' bullet near line 86 so it states that NAMED function pointers (Fn("name")) are now saved and rebound on load, while closures and curried function pointers that capture state are still skipped (with a chat message) because their captured state can't be reconstructed. Keep the surrounding 'Saved variables' section accurate. If a short code example helps, add one consistent with the file's style.

Run `cargo test --no-default-features` and `cargo clippy --no-default-features --all-targets`; confirm all tests pass and zero warnings. Commit onto branch `guh` with a conventional-commit message. Do NOT push.
acceptance_criteria: A named Rhai function pointer stored in a script variable is saved and restored across encode_vars/decode_vars, verified by a test asserting the restored value is a function pointer with the original name.

Closures and curried function pointers that capture state are still skipped and reported (not silently lost, not panicking), verified by a test asserting they appear in the skipped list with a clear reason.
Named function pointers nested inside arrays/maps round-trip (recursive path tested).
Existing script-variable saves (tags 0-8) still decode identically; the new tag is additive.
SCRIPTING.md accurately describes the new function-pointer persistence and the remaining closure limitation.
`cargo test --no-default-features` passes (>= FEAT-001 count + new tests); `cargo clippy --no-default-features --all-targets` is clean; Cargo.toml/Cargo.lock unchanged.
verification: Read the new tests and confirm the named-FnPtr round-trip test would fail if tag-9 encode or decode were removed, and the closure test confirms deterministic skip.
findings: Implemented tag-9 serialization for named Rhai FnPtrs in src/scripting.rs enc()/Dec::value(). Verified rhai 1.26.1 FnPtr API against registry source (/root/.cargo/registry/.../rhai-1.26.1/src/types/fn_ptr.rs): new(name)->RhaiResultOf, fn_name()->&str, is_curried()->bool, is_anonymous()->bool. Used d.read_lock::<rhai::FnPtr>() for detection (clean, no clone/cast). Closures are anonymous fns (is_anonymous()==true, name like 'anon$...' which FnPtr::new would reject anyway) and curried pointers (is_curried()==true) are deterministically skipped with descriptive messages. Updated existing variables_round_trip_through_bytes test (callback now round-trips, added a closure that is skipped) and added 3 tests: named_function_pointers_round_trip, named_function_pointers_round_trip_nested (array+map recursive path), closures_and_curried_pointers_are_skipped. SCRIPTING.md Saved-variables section updated. Results: cargo test --no-default-features = 243 passed (240 baseline + 3 new), clippy --no-default-features --all-targets = 0 warnings. NOTE: multiplayer::tests::wear_and_death_through_the_host is a wall-clock/sleep-based timing test that flaked once under full-suite load (passed in isolation and on a clean rerun both with and without my changes); it is unrelated to this serializer-only change. Cargo.toml/Cargo.lock untouched.
